#Session 3. importing genotype data

```{r}
#import synthetic genotype data into an R object dataframe
genotypes_df <- read.csv("../../common-disease-genomics-data/genotypes.csv")

```


#Analyse my genotype and indication pair in the synthetic data
```{r}
#select phenotype
my_indication <- select(phenotypes_df, c(subject_id, age_years, sex, ldl_mg_dl))

#select genotype
my_genotype <- select(genotypes_df, c(subject_id, PCSK9_rs11591147))

#join
my_gene_indication_pair <- left_join(my_indication, my_genotype, by="subject_id")

#rename your columns to something easier
my_gene_indication_pair <- my_gene_indication_pair %>% rename(LDL = "ldl_mg_dl", PCSK9_genotype ="PCSK9_rs11591147", age = "age_years")

#summarise the data subset by the three PCSK9 genotypes.
my_summary <- my_gene_indication_pair %>%
  group_by(PCSK9_genotype) %>%
  summarise(across(c(age, LDL), list(mean = mean, sd = sd)))

print(my_summary)

#perform some basic regression analyses
model_crude <- lm(LDL ~ PCSK9_genotype, data = my_gene_indication_pair)
summary(model_crude)

#the above produces output that is hard to understand. try this additional code from Claude:
#it uses the tbl_regression() function

tbl_regression(model_crude) |>
  add_glance_source_note() |>          # adds R², F-stat, etc. as a footer
  bold_p() |>                          # bolds p-values < 0.05
  bold_labels()

#now adjust for sex and age to reduce the spread or "variance" in the data and in case people of different ages and sex have slightly different distributions of genotypes (this could happen by chance in smaller datasets.
#perform some basic regression analyses
model_crude <- lm(LDL ~ PCSK9_genotype + age + sex, data = my_gene_indication_pair)
summary(model_crude)

#the above produces output that is hard to understand. try this additional code from Claude:
#it uses the tbl_regression() function

tbl_regression(model_crude) |>
  add_glance_source_note() |>          # adds R², F-stat, etc. as a footer
  bold_p() |>                          # bolds p-values < 0.05
  bold_labels()

#logistic regression for binary outcome
#first make a new variable, LDL_binary, where we split LDL into two catgories
my_gene_indication_pair$LDL_binary <- as.integer(my_gene_indication_pair$LDL > 100)
#just check what that looks like
table(my_gene_indication_pair$PCSK9_genotype, my_gene_indication_pair$LDL_binary)

#now run the logistic regression model (required when the outcome is binary (like a disease, 1,0 variable))
model <- glm(
  LDL_binary ~ PCSK9_genotype + age + sex,
  data   = my_gene_indication_pair
)
summary(model)


tbl_regression(model) |>
  add_glance_source_note() |>          # adds R², F-stat, etc. as a footer
  bold_p() |>                          # bolds p-values < 0.05
  bold_labels()

# Odds ratios (exponentiate coefficients)
exp(coef(model))

#create new variable that is LDLC in mmoll-1 not mg dl-1
my_gene_indication_pair$LDL_mmol <- my_gene_indication_pair$LDL / 38.67

#first make a new variable, LDL_binary, where we split LDL into two catgories
#first define your cut off
LDL_cutoff <- 4.0
#then define the new variable
my_gene_indication_pair$LDL_binary_mmol <- as.integer(my_gene_indication_pair$LDL_mmol > LDL_cutoff)
#just check what that looks like, printing out a descriptive heading.
print(paste("This table shows how the numbers of people with high cholesterol (>", LDL_cutoff, "mmoll-1) and low cholesterol are distributed across the 3 PCSK9 genotypes (0,1,2)"))
table(my_gene_indication_pair$PCSK9_genotype, my_gene_indication_pair$LDL_binary_mmol)

```


#code chunk to import real data from GWAS summary stats and investigate specific chromosomes
```{r}
#import real GWAS data from my INDICATION and the chromosome that contains the gene that encodes the TARGET protein
LDL_chr1_df <- read.csv("../../common-disease-genomics-data/GWAS_LDL_cholesterol/chr_LDL1.csv")

LDL_chr1_myregion_df <- LDL_chr1_df %>% filter(base_pair_location >55000000 & base_pair_location < 56000000)


#is the SNP used in the synthetic data present in the real GWAS data ?
LDL_chr1_mySNP_df <- LDL_chr1_myregion_df %>% filter(rsid == "rs11591147")
view(LDL_chr1_mySNP_df)


#now lets plot the effect of the key variant on the INDICATION, including the 95% confidence intervals (based on the standard error) using the ggplot2 function
# first calculate 95% CIs from the standard error
LDL_chr1_mySNP_df$ci_lower <- LDL_chr1_mySNP_df$beta - 1.96 * LDL_chr1_mySNP_df$standard_error
LDL_chr1_mySNP_df$ci_upper <- LDL_chr1_mySNP_df$beta + 1.96 * LDL_chr1_mySNP_df$standard_error

myplot <- ggplot(LDL_chr1_mySNP_df, aes(x = beta, y = reorder(rsid, beta))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Beta (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

print(myplot)
```

#locuszoomr plot
```{r}
# Locus plot using SLE GWAS data from Bentham et al 2015
# Using subset of data embedded in the package
library(locuszoomr)
data(SLE_gwas_sub)

library(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75)
loc <- locus(gene = 'UBE2L3', SLE_gwas_sub, flank = 1e5,
             ens_db = "EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75")
summary(loc)
locus_plot(loc)

# Or FTP download the full summary statistics from
# https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/studies/GCST003156
library(data.table)
SLE_gwas <- fread('../bentham_2015_26502338_sle_efo0002690_1_gwas.sumstats.tsv')

loc <- locus(gene = 'UBE2L3', SLE_gwas, flank = 1e5,
             ens_db = "EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75")
locus_plot(loc)


```





#This table describes the basic features of a synthetic dataset that includes phenotypes and genotypes generated by Claude. The relationship between genotypes and phenotypes is representative
```{r}
#calculate basic descriptive data and output to a table
#first for continuous data
age_stats <- summary(phenotypes_df$age_years)
bmi_stats <- summary(phenotypes_df$bmi_kg_m2)


continuous_stats <- rbind(age_stats, bmi_stats)
print(continuous_stats)


#this is Claude's suggestion on how to make the basic summary data look more professional.
#note that Claude uses "df" instead of the name of our df which is "phenotypes_df* and "age* instead of "age_years"
#so lets modify our dataframe names so that we do not need to modify Claude's code. 

df <- phenotypes_df %>% rename(age = "age_years", bmi = "bmi_kg_m2", disease1 = "cad_status", disease2 = "t2d_status")


#Claude code solution: 

# Summary stats
tbl <- rbind(
  "Age (years)"      = c(Mean=round(mean(df$age),1),   SD=round(sd(df$age),1),   "%"=""),
  "BMI (kg/m²)"     = c(Mean=round(mean(df$bmi),1),   SD=round(sd(df$bmi),1),   "%"=""),
  "Female sex"       = c(Mean="",                       SD="",                     "%"=paste0(round(mean(df$sex=="F")*100,1),"%")),
  "Hypertension"     = c(Mean="",                       SD="",                     "%"=paste0(round(mean(df$disease1)*100,1),"%")),
  "T2Diabetes"         = c(Mean="",                       SD="",                     "%"=paste0(round(mean(df$disease2)*100,1),"%"))
)

kable(tbl, caption="Table 1. Participant characteristics")



```
